> **Kshama Sawant - Seattle City Councilwoman**

black top, long red scarf, sunglasses, jeans. She speaks

### 1. Sawant - working the crowd

She never delivers a set piece to one camera position:

* **Constant turning and stepping.** She pivots 90 and then
180 degrees, back to camera at 379s, 423s, 497s, 554s, to
address the semi-circle in front of her, to her side and
behind her. The scarf swings with her.
* **Microphone gripped close, free hand doing the work.**
Chopping motions, open-palm appeals at 440-455s, jabbing
index finger at 507-530s, finger raised at 547s, 581s,
587s, fist/hand thrown up at 601-611s. At 426-436s she
points into the procession carrying the `STOP ARCTIC
DRILLING` banner as it passes behind her.
* **Face and voice projected.** Mouth opened very wide,
head up and thrown back, then breaking into a broad smile/
laugh at 349s, 383s, 517s before the next emphatic phrase.
Weight is forward, leaning toward listeners.

That is not reading, informing or mourning. Visually it is
high-arousal, confident, defiant and optimistic anger -
a rally speaker trying to mobilise people who are already
standing, applauding, photographing and holding banners
around her. The overlay put over her at 460-473s is
`May 18, 2015 Terminal 5 Seattle, WA / Peaceful Resistance
Against Arctic Drilling & Oil Rigs in Seattle`, and she
is the political peak of it.

### 2. The hand-off - energy drops

At **614s** the film cuts away from her close/medium shot
to a wide, static shot of the whole intersection. The next
person to take the microphone - long dark hair, dark top
and trousers, holding a clipboard/papers at 614-628s -
stands essentially in one spot, papers held against her
body, mic brought up with one hand, looking at the group
in front of her and at her notes. No striding, no 360-degree
turning, no pointing or fist raising.

The sequence that follows makes the change explicit:

* 628-678s: no oratory at all, slow pans over chalk on the
asphalt - `When is it ENOUGH?`, fish, a sun, a wind turbine.
* 678-685s: people sitting on the ground behind yellow tape,
listening.
* 685-718s: a man in a `save the arctic` sleeveless shirt
leads a chant/song through a megaphone that an older man
holds for him. He leans into the mouthpiece, other arm at
his side. The audience at 719-735s, with `350 Seattle` and
`7th GENERATION PRINCIPLE` signs, is seated on the road
singing back.

In other words the mood changes from Sawant's outward,
confrontational, fist-pointing mobilisation to a low-key,
stationary, communal and reflective one - procedural
announcing, creative art and call-and-response singing.
